answer: A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. Because the orchard sample is drawn from the mirror beacon, the cipher audit makes public the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is published per key. A random 20% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. That is 21 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
